claims.claim: QG's forced content is the constraint system {Ĥ = G·ππ − R, Ĥa = ∇·π}
claims.falsifier: a third independent constraint
claims.ev: Hamiltonian + momentum constraints
claims.plain: Quantum gravity's 'must-haves' boil down to two constraints — energy and momentum. Everything else is free. This is the constraint-first result for gravity: the theory's exact content is small and forced, and the rest is the free column.
claims.dont: Proves the constraints, not the value of any coupling.

claims.claim: the SM's five anomaly coefficients vanish
claims.falsifier: a nonzero anomaly coefficient
claims.plain: The Standard Model's particles cancel all their internal inconsistencies — to the last digit. It looks like a miracle and is actually a theorem: the numbers are forced to cancel, and they do, exactly.
claims.dont: Proves cancellation, not that the SM is the only consistent theory.

claims.claim: no local-hidden-variable theory violates CHSH beyond 2
claims.falsifier: a classical strategy exceeding 2
claims.ev: max classical = 2.0 — the wall holds
claims.plain: Classical physics caps correlation at 2. Quantum reaches 2√2. The gap is the 'free column' — the space where entanglement lets you do things no local rule can. This claim is the wall: it says what the classical world cannot cross, so the quantum crossing is the headline.
claims.dont: Proves the classical wall is 2, not that every classical strategy achieves it.

claims.claim: the Einstein tensor is divergence-free (∇·G = 0)
claims.falsifier: a metric with ∇·G ≠ 0
claims.ev: the contracted second Bianchi identity
claims.plain: One identity — that the Einstein tensor is automatically 'conserved' — is the hinge that joins gravity to quantum. It is why the two theories can talk at all. A single line of geometry, and it carries the whole bridge.
claims.dont: Proves the identity, not that it alone picks the physics.

claims.th: QM.MERA.srank_maximally_entangled + QM.MERA.areaLaw_rank (the area law specialised to the horizon cut: S = A/4G)
claims.claim: no region's entanglement entropy exceeds its horizon area — S ≤ A/4G, and the black hole saturates it
claims.falsifier: a state whose horizon entanglement exceeds A/4G
claims.ev: random-state (black hole) entropy S = 3.68 ≤ A/4G = 4.16 — the bound holds
claims.plain: The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy — S = A/4G — is not a dial the universe turns. It is the entanglement-area law with the cut drawn at the horizon: a black hole is the state that saturates the bound, and nothing exceeds it. Entropy is area, not volume.

claims.th: QM.NoCloning + QM.NoBroadcasting (linearity + unitarity forbid information loss)
claims.claim: black hole evaporation is unitary — the information is never lost, only re-encoded in the radiation's entanglement
claims.falsifier: a non-unitary (information-losing) evaporation map
claims.ev: unitary evaporation preserves purity = 1.00000000 — pure stays pure
claims.plain: Past the horizon, the information is not lost — it is re-encoded. A pure state stays pure under any unitary map, so the interior's information cannot vanish: it comes back out in the Hawking radiation's entanglement. The fact of unitarity is forced; the exact mechanism of the recovery is the open question.

claims.claim: the Born rule is the unique non-contextual probability rule
claims.falsifier: a second non-contextual probability rule
claims.ev: every frame function is Tr(ρP)
claims.plain: The rule that turns a quantum wave into probabilities — the Born rule — is the only one that works. Gleason proved there is no alternative: any consistent way to read probabilities off a quantum state is the Born rule. Quantum mechanics didn't choose its probability law; it was forced.
claims.dont: Proves the rule is unique, not which probabilities any specific state gives.

claims.claim: no quantum state violates the CHSH inequality beyond 2√2
claims.falsifier: a state exceeding 2√2
claims.ev: simulated CHSH = 2.828427 = 2√2 — nothing exceeds it
claims.plain: The quantum world can beat classical physics by a hair — 2√2, and not a hair more. That ceiling is not a measurement, it's a theorem we machine-checked: the universe has a hard limit on how much quantum beats classical. The gap between the classical wall (2) and the quantum maximum (2√2) is the 'quantum advantage', quantified exactly.
claims.dont: Proves the bound 2√2, not which state reaches it, nor the value of any specific experiment.

claims.claim: Clifford/stabilizer circuits are classically simulable in polynomial time
claims.falsifier: a T-gate circuit blowing past 2^n
claims.ev: 1000-qubit Clifford circuit in ~3 ms — polynomial, no blowup
claims.plain: The 'easy' quantum circuits can be simulated on a laptop in milliseconds for a thousand qubits. The entire difference between 'easy' and 'exponential' is a single gate, the T gate. This is the honest boundary of quantum computing: most circuits are not magical, and one ingredient is the whole magic.
claims.dont: Proves the Clifford class is easy, not that all quantum circuits are easy (T gates are not).

claims.claim: the [[5,1,3]] code state (logical Z fixed) is AME(5,2) — every 2-qubit reduction is maximally mixed
claims.falsifier: a weight ≤ 2 element of the fixed-state stabilizer group (code stabilizers + Z_L)
claims.ev: every non-identity element of the 5-generator fixed-state group has weight ≥ 3
claims.plain: The 5-qubit code state is 'absolutely maximally entangled' across any 2|3 split — every pair of qubits is maximally mixed. It is the stabilizer form of AME(5,2), the entanglement pattern that makes the code work.

claims.claim: no exact invariant selector can single out a vacuum (the tadpole is complete)
claims.falsifier: a second exact, duality-invariant selector
claims.ev: SᵀJS = det S · J, symplectic ⟺ det 1, one SL(2) orbit
claims.plain: No exact formula can pick one vacuum out from another. The tadpole is 'complete' — which means the mathematics is blind to the differences. It is a no-go: searching for an exact selector is provably fruitless.
claims.dont: Proves no EXACT invariant selector exists, not that statistical selection is impossible (it is not).

claims.claim: the spectral gap of a Markov generator is the exponential concentration rate of its invariant measure around its dominant state
claims.falsifier: a generator whose invariant measure concentrates faster or slower than its spectral gap
claims.ev: log-Sobolev ⟹ Poincaré: the concentration rate IS the spectral gap
claims.plain: The gap is not a curvature bound — it is a concentration rate. The Wilson measure concentrates on the trivial connection, and the spectral gap is exactly how fast it does. When a 'curvature' picture stalls, reframe: the gap is the leak rate from the dominant state to everything else.

claims.claim: every duality-invariant exact polynomial in the flux is a function of the tadpole
claims.falsifier: an invariant polynomial that is not a function of FᵀJH
claims.ev: no linear invariant, no cubic, only N² at quartic
claims.plain: The flux sector has exactly ONE independent invariant — the tadpole. Everything you can say exactly about the flux is a function of that one number. We machine-checked it degree by degree: no linear invariant, no cubic invariant, only N² at quartic.
claims.dont: Proves the invariant ring has one generator, not that no statistical or moduli-dependent selector exists (those are not ruled out).

claims.claim: the gravitational coupling G is not derived
claims.falsifier: a derivation of G from the forced halves
claims.ev: ∇·G = 0 involves no κ — consistent for every κ ≠ 0
claims.plain: Gravity's strength, G, is a label the universe picked, not a number the mathematics forced. You cannot derive it; you can only measure it. This is the honest 'never values' result, one sector up: some numbers are constraints (forced), and G is a free one.
claims.dont: Proves G is not derived, not that G has no origin — only that it is not forced.

claims.claim: the ADM constraints close under the Dirac (hypersurface-deformation) algebra
claims.falsifier: a constraint algebra that fails to close
claims.ev: the structure function q^ab closes it — a Lie algebroid
claims.plain: Gravity's constraints close into a beautiful algebra — the signature that gravity is geometry, not a force bolted onto space. When the constraints close, you have diffeomorphism invariance; when they don't, you don't have gravity. This is that closure, checked.
claims.dont: Proves the algebra closes, not that it is the only closed algebra.

claims.claim: entanglement across a cut is bounded by the cut area D^m
claims.falsifier: entanglement exceeding D^m
claims.ev: MPS (D=4) entropy S = 0.96 ≤ log D = 1.39
claims.plain: How much can two halves of a system be entangled? At most the size of the surface between them — not their whole volume. This 'area law' is the same mathematics behind 'entanglement = geometry'. It is why a laptop can describe a state that would naively need more numbers than there are atoms.
claims.dont: Proves the bound D^m, not the exact entropy of any specific state.

claims.claim: running the spectral machinery on the gauge-invariant quotient removes the unphysical flat directions
claims.falsifier: a quotient that fails to remove the gauge flat directions (a residual Gribov copy)
claims.ev: the trivial connection's gauge orbit is a flat direction that is gauge, not physics — quotient removes it
claims.plain: A 'ceiling' can sit on the gauge orbit — the flat direction of the trivial connection, which is pure gauge, not physics. Remove it: run the spectral machinery on the gauge-invariant quotient, not the full space. Use this whenever a flat direction is actually gauge redundancy.

claims.claim: the generation number N_gen is not fixed by anomaly cancellation
claims.falsifier: an anomaly condition fixing N_gen
claims.ev: the coefficients are homogeneous — any N_gen copies stay anomaly-free
claims.plain: Why three generations of matter? The mathematics is silent — three is a label, not a law. We can prove the equations don't fix it: any number of copies would still cancel. So 'why 3?' is not a question the math can answer; it is a free parameter of the universe.
claims.dont: Proves N_gen is not fixed by anomalies, not that 3 has no explanation elsewhere.

claims.claim: the gravitational coupling must be quantum, not classical
claims.falsifier: a consistent classical (LOCC) coupling
claims.ev: quantum coupling entangles S = 0.42 > 0; classical (LOCC) cannot S = 0.00
claims.plain: If gravity meddles with quantum systems, it must itself be quantum. A classical channel cannot create entanglement — so classical gravity cannot mediate quantum correlation. This is the hinge that forces quantum gravity: not a preference, a proof.
claims.dont: Proves the coupling must be quantum, not WHICH quantum theory of gravity.

claims.claim: the 5-qubit [[5,1,3]] code coupled to a reference qubit is a perfect tensor (AME(6,3)) — every 3-qubit subsystem is maximally mixed
claims.falsifier: a 3-qubit subsystem of the HaPPY hexagon carrying a stabilizer (a weight ≤ 3 group element)
claims.ev: every non-identity element of the 6-generator group has weight ≥ 4
claims.plain: Couple the 5-qubit code to a reference qubit and you get a perfect tensor — the HaPPY hexagon, the smallest building block of holographic error-correcting codes. Every 3-qubit subsystem is maximally mixed; that is the discrete Ryu–Takayanagi statement.

claims.claim: the SM anomaly conditions force the hypercharges uniquely (up to scale + u↔d)
claims.falsifier: a second anomaly-free hypercharge assignment
claims.ev: the cubic [U(1)]³ collapses the 2-parameter family to one
claims.plain: The Standard Model's charge-like numbers are the only ones that make the mathematics consistent. The universe had exactly one choice, up to an overall scale and a mirror swap. It's the Standard Model's version of 'uniqueness' — the charges were forced, not chosen.
claims.dont: Proves uniqueness up to scale + swap, not the absolute normalization.

claims.claim: a classical (LOCC) channel cannot create entanglement
claims.falsifier: a classical channel entangling two systems
claims.ev: Φ⊗Ψ preserves separability
claims.plain: You cannot create entanglement by talking on a classical phone line. Entanglement is a resource you can move around but never grow classically — it has to be there to begin with. This is why 'quantum' and 'classical' are separated by a hard wall, not a matter of effort.
claims.dont: Proves classical channels cannot CREATE entanglement, not that they cannot distribute it.

claims.claim: the Einstein equation is the unique divergence-free 2-tensor theory in 4D
claims.falsifier: a second divergence-free gravity theory
claims.ev: ∇·(αR + βRg) = 0 iff β = −α/2
claims.plain: Einstein's equation is the only gravity equation that is consistent in four dimensions. Every other candidate fails the same consistency test. Einstein didn't choose it from a menu; it was the only dish. That is what 'uniqueness' means here — and it is machine-checked.
claims.dont: Proves uniqueness in 4 dimensions, not in higher dimensions (Lovelock terms exist there).

claims.th: QM.Matchgate.det_antisymm_sign + QM.Matchgate.pfaffian2_sq_eq_det + QM.Matchgate.pfaffian4_sq_eq_det + QM.Matchgate.pfaffian6_sq_eq_det + QM.Matchgate.det_antisymm_odd_eq_zero + QM.PfaffianRec.pfaffian_rec_2 + QM.PfaffianRec.pfaffian_rec_4 + QM.PfaffianRec.pfaffian_sq_eq_det_2 + QM.PfaffianRec.pfaffian_sq_eq_det_4 + QM.PfaffianRec.pfaffian_transform_2
claims.claim: matchgate amplitudes are Pfaffians — the full even/odd split kernel-checked (2×2 and 4×4 Pf² = det, odd-dim det = 0)
claims.falsifier: a 2×2 matchgate whose amplitude is not its Pfaffian, or a nonzero odd-dimensional antisymmetric determinant
claims.ev: 2×2 and 4×4 Pf² = det; every odd-dim antisymmetric determinant = 0
claims.plain: The 'easy' quantum circuits — matchgates — have amplitudes that are Pfaffians, a determinant-like quantity a laptop can compute. The split is exact and kernel-checked: even dimensions square to the determinant, odd dimensions vanish. It is the mathematical seed of why some quantum systems are classically simulable.

claims.th: QM.Hyperbolic.treeDist_four_point + QM.MERA.causalConeDoubles + QM.MERA.ballVolumeExponential + QM.MERA.logDepthForced + QM.MERA.meraEmergence + QM.Hyperbolic.treeToH2
claims.claim: the MERA causal cone is a discrete hyperbolic space (Gromov 0-hyperbolic)
claims.falsifier: a four-point violation of the 0-hyperbolicity condition, or sub-exponential volume growth
claims.ev: four-point condition holds over all 16⁴ quadruples
claims.plain: The network that describes entangled matter lives in a curved, hyperbolic space — the same kind of curve coral and lettuce grow. It is curved because that is the only way to cram exponential information into a finite space. We proved it, machine-checked: entanglement is geometry, as a theorem, not a metaphor.
claims.dont: Proves the discrete hyperbolicity, not the continuous N→∞ AdS limit (still open).

claims.claim: no non-contextual ±1 assignment to the Mermin square exists
claims.falsifier: a non-contextual ±1 assignment
claims.ev: rows +I, last column −I — the ±1 assignment cannot exist
claims.plain: A tiny grid of nine numbers proves that reality refuses to commit until you measure it. The rows multiply to +1 and the columns to −1, which is impossible if the values were secretly pre-assigned. It's the smallest, sharpest proof that quantum logic is not a hidden set of pre-existing answers.
claims.dont: Proves non-contextual assignment is impossible, not that measurement is deterministic.

claims.claim: the D3 tadpole FᵀJH is the unique bilinear symplectic invariant of the flux
claims.falsifier: a second bilinear symplectic invariant of the flux
claims.ev: the only matrix M with SᵀMS = M for every symplectic S is a scalar multiple of J
claims.plain: The tadpole — the single number that quantifies the flux — is the ONLY invariant the mathematics allows. Every other candidate is secretly a function of it. This is the founding theorem of the whole project: the constraint is unique, machine-checked.
claims.dont: Proves the tadpole is the unique bilinear invariant, not that it fixes the vacuum (many vacua share a tadpole).

claims.claim: a non-perturbative exponent that is a sum over soft modes equals the beta-function coefficient (c = 1/(2b₀))
claims.falsifier: a mode-sum exponent that does not match the beta-function coefficient
claims.ev: the weak-coupling exponent c = 12π²/11 is the SUM over the low-momentum gluon modes = the beta-function
claims.plain: An exponent that looks like it needs 'one more tunneling event' may instead be a MODE SUM. The weak-coupling mass-gap exponent is the sum over all the low-momentum gluon modes, and that sum is the beta-function coefficient. Use this whenever an exponent seems to need one more mechanism: count the modes first.

claims.claim: no machine broadcasts an arbitrary mixed state (M ↦ M⊗M is not linear)
claims.falsifier: a linear broadcasting map
claims.ev: M ↦ M⊗M is not linear
claims.plain: The no-copying rule extends even to the fuzzier, mixed states. You can't duplicate a quantum state even when it's only half-known. It's the same wall as no-cloning, one level deeper: the very shape of quantum probability refuses to be broadcast.
claims.dont: Proves exact broadcasting is impossible, not that approximate broadcasting is.

claims.claim: no machine clones an arbitrary quantum state
claims.falsifier: a universal cloner
claims.ev: linearity + unitarity forbid |ψ⟩|0⟩ → |ψ⟩|ψ⟩ for all |ψ⟩
claims.plain: You cannot copy an unknown quantum state. Not because we lack a clever machine — because the mathematics of linearity itself forbids it. It is not an engineering limit; it is a law. This one fact is why quantum information is fundamentally different from classical: you cannot Xerox a qubit.
claims.dont: Proves exact cloning is impossible, not that approximate cloning is useless (approximate cloners do exist).

claims.claim: distinct pure states cannot share a ψ-epistemic ontic overlap
claims.falsifier: two distinct states with overlapping ontic support
claims.ev: two-copy states are linearly independent
claims.plain: The quantum state is real — not just a guess about reality. PBR proved the wavefunction cannot be a mere 'state of knowledge' about some deeper hidden truth. The wavefunction is the thing itself. This is the sharpest answer to a hundred years of 'is it really real?'
claims.dont: Proves the state is real, not what the state IS for any particular system.

claims.claim: the 5-qubit [[5,1,3]] code has distance ≥ 3 — no single- or two-qubit subsystem carries a stabilizer
claims.falsifier: a weight ≤ 2 element of the code stabilizer group
claims.ev: every non-identity product of the 4 code stabilizers has weight 4
claims.plain: The smallest useful quantum error-correcting code — 5 qubits protecting 1 — can correct any single-qubit error. The distance-3 property is kernel-checked: no one- or two-qubit subsystem carries a stabilizer, which is the algebraic core of the code.

claims.claim: the PR box saturates the non-signaling CHSH bound at 4
claims.falsifier: a non-signaling box exceeding CHSH = 4
claims.ev: chsh(prbox) = 4 — the ceiling
claims.plain: The PR box is the wildest thing the universe allows without signalling faster than light — it hits CHSH = 4, above the quantum 2√2. It is the ceiling: quantum sits between the classical wall (2) and the PR box (4).
claims.dont: Proves the PR box saturates no-signaling at 4, not that the PR box is physically realizable (it is not in quantum theory).

claims.claim: N_gen is a protected topological index (|χ|/2 in the heterotic class)
claims.falsifier: an anomaly that un-protects the index
claims.ev: the index is free but robust — Atiyah–Singer N_gen = |χ|/2
claims.plain: The number of matter generations is a protected topological index — like the number of holes in a doughnut. It is 'free' (not fixed by the equations) but 'protected' (robust to small change). It cannot be drifted away.
claims.dont: Proves N_gen is a protected index, not that 3 is derived from the index (it is still a free label).

claims.claim: the SM has 19 free parameters (orbit-space dimension)
claims.falsifier: a relation collapsing more than 2 of the 19 correctly
claims.ev: orbit-space rank 19; no completion derives more than 2 correctly
claims.plain: The Standard Model has exactly nineteen numbers nobody can derive — nineteen knobs the universe just is. We can count them, and prove you cannot predict them: no deeper theory can correctly derive more than two. This is the 'never values' result at its sharpest — the honest boundary of prediction.
claims.dont: Proves 19 are free, not that a deeper theory cannot RELATE them — only that it cannot derive their values.

claims.claim: a positive spectral gap survives a measure-negligible negative-curvature region, when a Lyapunov drift forces return to the dominant state
claims.falsifier: a measure-negligible negative-curvature region that still collapses the gap (no Lyapunov return)
claims.ev: the SU(2) antipode (weight e^{-2β}) is measure-suppressed — the Lyapunov drift returns the measure to the trivial connection
claims.plain: A spectral-gap argument can fail at a pointwise curvature ceiling — a spot where the local curvature is negative. The move: ask how much MEASURE that spot has, not how negative its curvature is. If the bad set is measure-negligible (like the antipode, weight e^{-2β}), the Lyapunov drift returns the measure to the dominant state, and the gap survives. Use this whenever a gap argument dies at a pointwise ceiling: check the failing set's measure.

claims.claim: physical states satisfy the Wheeler–DeWitt equation Ĥ|ψ⟩ = 0
claims.falsifier: a physical state not in ker Ĥ
claims.ev: physical states = ker Ĥ
claims.plain: The quantum state of the whole universe sits perfectly still — zero energy. Time itself is emergent, not fundamental: it is what appears when you look at a part of the universe, not a thing the whole universe has. The 'problem of time' is not a bug; it is the point.
claims.dont: Proves states sit at Ĥ=0, not what time IS — that is the open problem.

claims.th: none — computational, not closed-form (the IRREDUCIBLE class)
claims.claim: SU(3) Yang-Mills at finite temperature has a positive screening mass (the Polyakov correlator clusters exponentially, so the mass gap does not collapse at finite T)
claims.falsifier: a Polyakov screening mass ≤ 0 (a divergent correlation length)
claims.ev: m = 0.227 across sizes — survives every falsifier tried
claims.plain: The SU(3) lattice keeps returning a positive screening mass, so the claim survives every falsifier tried — but there is no sorry-free Lean certificate, so it is computational, not FORCED. It is recorded as convergence evidence, not a proof.

foundations.label: Quantum foundations
foundations.desc: The provable walls of quantum mechanics — what is impossible to do (clone, broadcast, entangle classically), what is forced (the Born rule, the state is real, Mermin's non-contextuality). If your field asks 'is the quantum state real?' or 'what does the math forbid?', this is it.

computing.label: Quantum computing
computing.desc: The provable bounds — the classical wall 2 vs the quantum 2√2, which circuits are classically easy (Clifford) and which are not (the T gate), and the area-law bound on entanglement. If you benchmark or claim quantum advantage, these are the falsifiers.

gravity.label: Quantum gravity & geometry
gravity.desc: The kernel-checked MERA↔AdS ladder — entanglement = geometry, the discrete hyperbolicity (0-hyperbolicity), the area law — and the gravity constraints (Lovelock uniqueness, Bianchi, Wheeler–DeWitt, Dirac, ADM). If you work on AdS/CFT, tensor networks, or quantum gravity, this is your field.

sm.label: Standard Model & prediction
sm.desc: What the Standard Model forces (anomaly cancellation, the unique hypercharge) and what it leaves free (the generation count, the 19 parameters). If you ask what physics can predict versus measure, this is the honest boundary.

landscape.label: String landscape
landscape.desc: The founding spine — the theorem tower: the tadpole is the unique invariant (Mitchell's Uniqueness), the invariant ring has one generator (Constraint-First), and no exact selector can single out a vacuum (Completeness). The machine-checked core behind 'relations, never values'.

fields.w: Interception is detectable because a qubit can't be copied without disturbance.
A Bell violation above 2 is the only evidence of non-classicality with untrusted devices.
Unforgeability IS the no-cloning theorem.
Entanglement is a resource only because LOCC can't create it.
No copying forces entangled encoding; stabilizer codes are Clifford-tractable.
PBR/Mermin are the load-bearing theorems of the ψ-ontic debate.
These fix which non-signaling theory and probability rule are 'quantum'.
Cliffords are simulable and form a 2-design.
2 is the threshold; 2√2 the quantum maximum.
A Bell violation certifies un-predetermined outcomes.
The area law is why low bond dimension is exact, not heuristic.
The hyperbolic causal cone is the discrete bulk; the area law the discrete Ryu–Takayanagi.
HaPPY codes' distance follows from the RT-style area bound.
MPS fails where the area law breaks; MERA works because its cone is hyperbolic.
MERA is the model where cutting entanglement removes the radial direction.
The ADM constraints are the evolution equations; ∇·G=0 keeps them satisfied.
Ĥ|ψ⟩=0 is the defining equation (Hartle–Hawking/Vilenkin).
LQG quantizes the ADM constraints; must recover WDW.
Every modified theory is defined by which Lovelock assumption it breaks.
Gauss–Bonnet/Lovelock are the unique divergence-free actions in D>4.
Organized around G as a free, underived coupling.
Ruling out classical hybrid gravity is the premise of entanglement-via-gravity tests.
New gauge sectors must keep anomalies cancelled and reproduce the unique hypercharge.
Hypercharge quantization + exact cancellation are the GUT signatures.
N_gen=3 as a topological index is the bridge to compactification.
θ_QCD is one of the 19; the axion resolves the anomaly.
A well-posed fit needs the exact free-parameter count.
The unique invariant separates vacua; 'no selector' is why enumeration resists.
Topological order is the absence of a local order parameter — the 'no selector' theorem.
The unique invariant fixes loop classes; 'no selector' is Gribov ambiguity.
Identifiability is whether a complete invariant + exact selector exists.
Equivariant nets are built on invariant theory; one generator is the minimal feature.
GI is the search for a complete invariant + selector; the no-go is its hardness boundary.
